description: Ham Radio Village at DEF CON 27 covers radio frequency security and amateur radio techniques with 2 talks on RF security and antenna design.

talks.title: The RF Dark Arts
talks.summary:
In this talk at the DEF CON 27 Ham Radio Village, Jason (W2LDU) demystifies the world of amateur radio and software-defined radio (SDR) for hackers, exploring how entry-level radio frequencies provide an expansive playground for exploration. He opens by discussing the process of earning an FCC amateur radio license at 03:00, highlighting that much of the technician exam focuses on fundamental electronics, circuits, and radio wave propagation. He also showcases how digital modes like APRS (Automatic Packet Reporting System) operate at 06:00, allowing radio operators to beacon telemetry, GPS coordinates, and messages over VHF frequencies.

Jason then compares radio hardware options at 09:00, contrasting budget handheld transceivers like Baofengs with flexible RTL-SDR dongles. At 12:00, he demonstrates how an affordable USB software-defined radio receiver can monitor unencrypted transmissions across hundreds of megahertz, including ADS-B signals broadcast by commercial aircraft transponders and live weather telemetry from NOAA polar-orbiting satellites. At 15:00, he explains how regional repeater networks and linked repeater systems enable wide-area point-to-point communication across hundreds of miles.

Concluding with practical operational advice, Jason runs a live spectrum waterfall demonstration at 21:00 to illustrate how to visually identify signals across active frequency bands. At 24:00, he shares open-source decoding tools and community resources, encouraging hackers to join local ham radio clubs and experiment with SDR listening to master the radio frequency spectrum.
